page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a total of 144 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration, though it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across several areas. Single-core processing is highly efficient, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly capable, with write operations on large blocks reaching top-tier status and read operations ranking in the top 25%. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier performance for both prompt processing and text generation using small (135M) and medium (7B) models, though data is unavailable for large 70B models.

The server offers high resource density for GPU-intensive tasks, making it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads that can leverage parallel processing across three L40S GPUs. However, a notable tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions. The shared CPU allocation may also introduce variability under sustained multi-tenant loads, despite the strong CPU benchmarks. This configuration is highly suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning training, image processing, and parallel scientific computing.
